use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

claims.content: C2 JU
All IUs must be capable of periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
The C2 JU must recognize that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation before initiating resolution action.
Correlation rules applied must be in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1 (Air and Surface Track Correlation).
Each C2 JU must have automatic correlation capability for real-time air or surface tracks to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

Operational contingency constraints (OCCs) such as engagement status, pending commands, controlled track status, or IU activity state must be evaluated for each track, as they may restrict correlation unless an exception applies.
The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

claims.content: Receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
When the RV field is set to value 0, it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable; when set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.

If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed as an exception to OCC restrictions.
If a selection conflict occurs due to Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.

Receiving C2 JUs shall not accept the requested correlation if there is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g (e.g., engagement status, pending commands, controlled track). In this case, the correlation shall be rejected.
If the Retained TN and Dropped TN would decorrelate when subjected to decorrelation criteria, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1 (indicating reverse correlation is rejected), the correlation shall be rejected.
If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.

C2 JUs receiving a manually initiated correlation (RV=3) shall reject the request if the two tracks are of a different E/C, have an existing E/C conflict, one is simulated and the other live, or both are locally derived real-time tracks.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the receiving JU shall transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If the originating C2 JU holds R-squared for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message; if the JU does not hold the Dropped TN, it shall take no further action.
The recognizing C² JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks, identifying the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions exist which require or allow rejection or a reverse correlation request.
If the originating C² JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, it drops the Dropped TN and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
If own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN is designated as a common local track upon execution of the correlation.
If own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is transmitted for the Dropped TN.

The correlation is deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request, and all associated processing is cancelled.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the receiving JU transmits a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.
